classification.difficultyReason: Use the nonnegative domain to factor out square root x or simplify after squaring, then isolate the unknown and rationalise; the shared radical makes this a routine linked surd calculation.

answer.short:
$x=10+2\sqrt{21}$.

Square both sides, simplify using $x\geq0$, and check the result in the original equation.
answer.worked:
The radicals require $x\geq0$. Squaring both sides gives
$$\begin{align*}(\sqrt{7x}-\sqrt{3x})^2&=16\\7x+3x-2\sqrt{21x^2}&=16\\(10-2\sqrt{21})x&=16\\x&=\frac{8}{5-\sqrt{21}}\\x&=\frac{8(5+\sqrt{21})}{25-21}\\x&=10+2\sqrt{21}.\end{align*}$$
Check in the original equation:
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{7x}-\sqrt{3x}&=\sqrt{70+14\sqrt{21}}-\sqrt{30+6\sqrt{21}}\\\sqrt{7x}-\sqrt{3x}&=(7+\sqrt{21})-(3+\sqrt{21})\\\sqrt{7x}-\sqrt{3x}&=4.\end{align*}$$
Hence $x=10+2\sqrt{21}$ is the solution.
